targetText:
Future society will be socialist society. This means primarily, that there will 
be no classes in that society; there will be neither capitalists nor proletarians 
and, consequently, there will be no exploitation. In that society there will be 
only workers engaged in collective labour.
summary: Future socialist society abolishes class divisions, commodity exchange, and capitalist wage labor.
explanation: Outlines the economic foundation of communism: private ownership of means of production is replaced by collective social ownership. With the elimination of capitalist exploitation, production for market profit is replaced by direct production for human need.

targetText:
The socialist dictatorship of the proletariat, capture of power by the 
proletariat: this is what the socialist revolution must start with.
summary: The conquest of state power and dictatorship of the proletariat is the necessary starting point of revolution.
explanation: Socialist revolution cannot bypass state power as anarchists advocate. The working class must capture state power and establish its own dictatorship to suppress counter-revolutionary resistance and expropriate the means of production from the capitalist class.
topics: The State and Dictatorship of the Proletariat

targetText:
That is to say, the dictatorship of the proletariat will be a dictatorship of 
the entire proletariat as a class over the bourgeoisie and not the domination of 
a few individuals over the proletariat.
summary: The dictatorship of the proletariat represents the democratic rule of the armed working class, modeled on the Paris Commune.
explanation: Rebuts the anarchist charge that Marxist dictatorship means rule by a few elite bureaucrats. Citing Engels and the Paris Commune, Stalin demonstrates that the proletarian dictatorship is the organized self-defense and governance of the armed working class over the defeated exploiters.
topics: The State and Dictatorship of the Proletariat
context: Following the defeat of the 1871 Paris Commune, bourgeois commentators and anarchists attacked the concept of proletarian dictatorship, prompting Marx and Engels to point to the Commune's direct democracy as its historical living model.
